comparison.question: When does excitation redirect nuclear motion?

comparison.mission_link: Possible photochemical energy conversion; no efficiency prediction
comparison.integration: WorldSpec nuclei plus electronic amplitudes and coupling/force bridge
comparison.computable_inputs: Electronic energies and gradients through supported quantum-chemistry interfaces
comparison.assumptions: Surface truncation, classical nuclei in surface hopping, decoherence model
comparison.observables: Surface populations and nuclear coordinates, subject to trajectory interpretation

comparison.reuse: Many photoactive molecules, conditional on interface support

comparison.computable_inputs: Selected molecular response quantities; bath spectrum requires additional evidence

comparison.reuse: Broad given independently grounded bath models
comparison.falsifier: Arbitrary decay constants would not answer material-environment question

comparison.question: Is apparent transfer actual charge separation or a partition artefact?
comparison.mission_link: Potential photovoltaics/catalysis connection, not device qualification
comparison.mature_engine: PySCF response/CI or a mature dynamics engine depending on question
comparison.integration: Fragment definitions plus electronic-state and observable bridge
comparison.computable_inputs: Electronic integrals, densities and transition densities
comparison.assumptions: Fragment partition, model states, missing nuclear/bath processes

comparison.new_freedom: Full determinant superposition and two-particle reduced density in a finite orbital space
comparison.question: How does singlet correlation change local double occupancy and spin correlations beyond restricted Hartree-Fock?
comparison.scientific_value: Makes charge/spin correlation observable rather than inferring it from orbital energies
comparison.mission_link: Electronic bonding and correlated-material mechanisms may inform future energy research; no X or material discovery claim
comparison.integration: Existing WorldSpec RHF reference plus explicit FCI model, immutable CI/RDM arrays, existing bounded nuclear displacement
comparison.computable_inputs: All one/two-electron Coulomb integrals from specified nuclei and basis
comparison.assumptions: Fixed nuclei, nonrelativistic electronic Hamiltonian, STO-3G finite space and defined Lowdin partition
comparison.observables: Correlation energy, natural occupations, double occupancy, connected charge covariance, singlet spin correlations
comparison.current_feasibility: H4 has 4 spatial orbitals and 36 alpha/beta determinants; audited mature implementation, no new solver
comparison.reuse: Adapter accepts bounded closed-shell H assemblies, not hard-coded H4 solver; broader chemistry remains unqualified
comparison.falsifier: SCF/FCI failure, RDM/energy inconsistency or near-idempotent density invalidates expected strong-correlation interpretation

selection_reason: Not merely cheaper energy refinement: a many-electron state with non-Wick two-particle observables opens questions unavailable in the current single-determinant/two-state world. Its Coulomb parameters are computed in one system rather than fitted or borrowed across systems. The bounded real-integral model is scientifically interpretable though minimal-basis accuracy is not established.

first_experiment.object: Neutral H4 open line, z = [-2.25,-0.75,0.75,2.25] angstrom
first_experiment.model: RHF reference and spin-singlet full CI, STO-3G, same fixed-nuclei electronic Hamiltonian
first_experiment.prediction: E_FCI-E_RHF < -0.001 Eh and sum_i n_i(2-n_i)>0.05; both thresholds are scientific forecasts, not numerical acceptance criteria
first_experiment.falsifier: A numerically valid result failing either threshold weakens the predicted non-single-determinant character; retain it without adjusting thresholds
first_experiment.observables: Natural occupations; Lowdin-site double occupancy and spin/charge correlations versus the same-partition RHF Wick baseline
first_experiment.boundary: RHF is not the best unrestricted determinant; negative pair correlation alone is not beyond-mean-field evidence. Local quantities are partition-dependent. No bulk phase, dynamics, material precision or human novelty claim.

second_experiment: NOT_SELECTED. Only after actual first observation, current Work AI may select one existing DISPLACE_ATOM action of norm <=0.05 angstrom along z, keeping composition/charge/spin/basis/FCI fixed, or STOP. No parameter is prewritten.

resource_proposal.sequence: First frozen geometry; second only after reading and freezing an actual AI decision
